newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-IPE Brent seen up but needs to hold gains.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-IPE Brent seen up but needs to hold gains.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20 IPE BRENT 18.18 * 17.70 * 18.45 * 49 * 17.93 * 18.00

* Analysts expect a continuation of the strength seen last week with a firm base at $17.49 and resistance coming in at $18.45. * A substantial and prolonged break through resistance by Brent will be needed to confirm an uptrend in place.
IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures are seen rising on Monday but a substantial and prolonged break through resistance by Brent will be needed to confirm an uptrend in place, analysts said.

Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson, Isle of Man saw the market continuing the strength seen late last week with a firm base in at $17.49 and first resistance coming in at $18.45 last Wednesday's high which represents a 0.318 Fibonacci retracement.

"The next short term target would then be $19 for 'roundaphobes' which marks a 50 percent Fibonacci retracement," Wilson said. "In the longer term the congested period in the $19.20-70 region on the August chart could be a target, but I don't see an new contract highs for a while.".
Al Graham at Elliott Wave international said in his daily report that the market's current choppy trading fashion is keeping confidence in the short term picture low.
"Tentatively the $18.45 high ended a corrective rally from $17.49, arguing the rise from $17.83 will reverse hard from below $18.45 and keep heading down to the $17.49 low," Graham said.

However, he said confidence to the downside will not be strong until $17.70 support gives way. "The bigger picture we're looking for is the last leg down from a major bottom. A move above $18.45 now would force consideration that one is already in place".
IPE Brent was called to open around 10-15 cents higher.
"It shouldn't have any problems making the call. The crude markets over here are tight and this (Iraqi) news helps the push upwards," one broker said.

On gas oil Graham said, "The corrective rise appears to be nearing completion but we may see one more leg up toward the $165.50-75 area before it is completed. But all it will take is a drop through trendline and structural support in the $162-$160.75 area to make a strong case for new lows below $158."
Wilson saw minor support at $159.50 with key support at $158 while last week's $164.50 high was significant following a double top at the level earlier in the month.
"Above this is the tiny chart gap to $164.75 but more significantly the gap between $170.75 and $171.50 will be the first objective with a ceiling around $175," Wilson said.
August Brent crude was bid at $18.29 per barrel on SIMEX after London settled at $18.18 for a gain of 33 cents on Friday.
Brokers said Iraqi comments that exports would not resume as soon as had been expected would support prices.

Iraq's chief United Nations negotiator, Abdul Amir al-Anbari, said in Switzerland at the weekend that exports might resume in August so long as Baghdad's distribution plan for medicine and food was approved during July by the U.N..
August NYMEX crude on ACCESS was valued around $19.57, up 11 cents from New York's close.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
